message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of solid leg‑building moves you can mix into your routine—whether you’re just starting out or looking to add variety for more advanced training:

| Exercise | Primary Muscles Targeted | Key Tips |
|----------|--------------------------|----------|
| **Squat** (bodyweight, goblet, barbell back/ front) | Quadriceps, glutes, hamstrings, core | Keep knees tracking over toes; depth depends on mobility |
| **Lunge** (forward, reverse, walking, stationary) | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Step long enough so the back knee almost touches the floor |
| **Deadlift** (conventional, sumo, Romanian) | Hamstrings, glutes, lower back, traps | Maintain neutral spine; hinge at hips |
| **Leg Press** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Adjust foot placement to emphasize quads (high) or glutes (low) |
| **Calf Raise** (standing, seated, single‑leg) | Gastrocnemius, soleus | Full range of motion; pause at top and bottom |
| **Step‑Up** (onto bench or box) | Glutes, quads, hamstrings | Drive through the heel of the stepping leg |
| **Bulgarian Split Squat** | Quads, glutes, hamstrings | Use dumbbells or bodyweight; keep torso upright |
| **Hamstring Curl** (lying or seated machine) | Hamstrings | Slow eccentric phase for better activation |
| **Glute Bridge / Hip Thrust** | Glutes, hamstrings, lower back | Squeeze glutes at the top; avoid arching the lower back |
| **Box Jump / Plyometric Jump** | Power in quads, glutes, calves | Focus on soft landing; start with low height |

### How to Structure a Leg Workout
1. **Warm‑up** – 5–10 min cardio + dynamic stretches (leg swings, hip circles).  
2. **Compound lifts first** – Squats, deadlifts, or leg press (3–4 sets × 6–12 reps).  
3. **Accessory work** – Lunges, step‑ups, glute bridges (3 sets × 8–15 reps).  
4. **Isolation & finishing** – Calf raises, hamstring curls (3 sets × 12–20 reps).  
5. **Cool‑down** – Light stretching or foam rolling.

Feel free to swap in variations or adjust rep ranges based on whether you’re focusing on strength (lower reps, heavier weight) or hypertrophy/endurance (higher reps, moderate weight). Happy training!
